solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Envisaged either part of iron tool

indicators.note: something that is part of another sits inside it, so the iron wraps around the 'either' word

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
the partner word in the pair 'either ... or'
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Someone pictures one half of some iron implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Either part' means the word that partners either in the pair either/or; Fe is iron's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To have foreseen something is to have pictured it in advance, so the two past-tense verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Priest carrying English carol-singer, we hear, who's very light

indicators.note: a priest carrying something holds it within, so the English letter goes inside

parts.note: a Catholic priest is addressed as Father
standard abbreviation for English

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the carol-singer word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: waits were bands of carol-singers going from house to house at Christmas

explanation.surface: A priest helping a frail chorister along on the carol round.
explanation.walkthrough: FATHER holding E gives FEATHER; the waits are the old British name for street carol-singers, a word that sounds like WEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A featherweight boxer is in one of the lightest divisions, and figuratively the word describes anyone of little heft.

clue.text: Celebration of one side, each grabbing the other

parts.note: right is one of the two sides

indicators.note: a word that grabs something takes hold of it and keeps it inside itself

parts.note: each and every mean the same
having used right, the other side is left

explanation.surface: A party held by one faction in which every member snatches at the opposing camp.
explanation.walkthrough: R comes first, then EVERY grabbing L: R + EVE(L)RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelry is lively merrymaking, the noisy enjoyment that goes with a festive celebration.

clue.text: Add water to bouquet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to sprinkle with a fine mist of liquid
second meaning: a noun, a small bunch of flowers

explanation.surface: A florist's instruction to freshen up a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the act of misting something with water and a small posy or sprig of blooms.

clue.text: Most bizarre couple holding hands that is separated by monarch

parts.note: in bridge, West and East are a couple of hands that partner each other

indicators.note: when something separates a phrase it pushes in between its parts, so the monarch sits inside

parts.note: the Latin id est, abbreviated i.e.
R for rex or regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: An odd image of a pair walking hand in hand split apart by a king.
explanation.walkthrough: The bridge partners W and E come first; then ID EST is split by R, giving I-R-D EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Weird means strange, so the superlative is the strangest or most bizarre of a set.

clue.text: Capital: something that constricts gains acquired

indicators.note: a word that gains something takes it in, so the second piece is placed inside

parts.note: the boa constrictor kills by squeezing its prey
to have got something is to have acquired it

explanation.surface: A business note about a squeeze on profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gains acquired' reads like a financial phrase, but gains is the container signal and acquired gives GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the capital city of Colombia in South America.

clue.text: Heard why I rested in bunk like some children

indicators.note: something that rests in a place lies inside it

parts.note: bunk and bosh both mean nonsense
taken as written

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the word by its sound, so it stands for a letter pronounced the same

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like the word why

explanation.surface: Someone asks why they took a nap in a bunk bed, as children do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' suggests a bed, but it means nonsense here. Y and I go inside BOSH.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyish means typical of young lads, so it describes the manner of some youngsters, the boys.

clue.text: Evangelist takes turn with person delivering letters

parts.note: your go is your turn in a game
someone who spells out letters, not a postman

explanation.surface: A preacher shares a round with the postman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person delivering letters' points at a postman; it is someone who spells words out letter by letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A gospeller is a preacher of the gospel, which is exactly what an evangelist does.

clue.text: Prepare for match maybe, running around on rising ground

indicators.note: a word running around another encircles it, holding it inside

parts.note: athletes train before a match

indicators.note: in a down clue a word that rises is read from bottom to top, back to front

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a memo

explanation.surface: An athlete getting ready for a game by jogging round on an uphill slope.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, rising reads the short word upward; it lands just after the first letter of the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrain is a stretch of land considered for its physical features, a synonym for ground.

clue.text: A mixture with one left out — bad luck

indicators.note: one is the numeral I, and leaving it out means removing that letter

parts.note: taken as written
a mixture or variety

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe missing an ingredient, which is unfortunate.
explanation.walkthrough: DIVERSITY loses its first I after A is put in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Adversity means hardship or misfortune, the run of difficult circumstances people call ill fortune.

clue.text: Band in performance that's barely finished

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a long narrow piece of material
second meaning: a striptease, an act that ends with the performer nearly naked

explanation.surface: A musical group whose show was only just completed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely finished' sounds like 'only just finished' but means finishing bare.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a narrow length of cloth or land, and also a show of undressing on stage.

clue.text: Like rook moves, perhaps, what's odd about king and pawn finish after I moved?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer word goes round the chess pieces
moving one letter rearranges the word, so the I shifts to a new place

parts.note: peculiar means odd
R for rex, king
P is the chess notation for pawn
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A chess puzzle: what is strange about king and pawn endings after a move?
explanation.walkthrough: Only one letter moves in the odd word, one place earlier; the chess pieces then slot in after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rook travels along ranks and files, which meet at right angles, so its moves can be at right angles to each other.

clue.text: Festive decoration, quite neglected by wife

indicators.note: neglected means left out, so the letter for wife is dropped

parts.note: quite in the sense of completely
standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: The Christmas decorations have been rather ignored by the wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite' reads as 'rather', but here it means completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprigs of the evergreen with red berries are traditionally hung up at Christmas time.

clue.text: Democrat's relating to nonvoters in state needing attention

parts.note: standard abbreviation for Democrat
the 's read as a contraction of is
re means concerning
in Parliament a pair is two members of opposing sides who agree both to abstain

explanation.surface: A US political note: a Democrat talks about non-voters in a state that needs focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like an American state, but it is part of the definition. Pairing is a Westminster arrangement letting two opposing MPs miss a vote without changing the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is a run-down condition, a building in such a condition needs mending and upkeep.

clue.text: Republican's opponent in solitary, mistreated

indicators.note: letters that are mistreated are knocked about into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An enemy of the republic held in solitary confinement and badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Republican' suggests the US party, but here it means an anti-monarchist.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist supports keeping a monarchy, the cause a republican wants to abolish.

clue.text: Old-fashioned computing aid to record sound of a cadence

parts.note: to log something is to record it

indicators.note: sound of tells us to take how the phrase is spoken and spell that differently

parts.note: a cadence is a rhythm

explanation.surface: A musician uses an outdated calculator to note down a rhythmic pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: Tables of these, and slide rules built on them, did calculations before electronic calculators.
explanation.definitionFit: Before pocket calculators, printed tables of these values were used to turn multiplication into addition.

clue.text: Look for a second good weapon

parts.note: standard abbreviation for good
a long spear used by knights

explanation.surface: Someone hunting for a backup weapon that is any good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a second' feels like 'for a backup', but it belongs to the definition: a look lasting only a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A glance is a quick, brief look that lasts only a moment.

clue.text: Got ready for dance she rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged means put in a different order, so these letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman prepared herself for the dance by doing her hair again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got ready' looks like 'prepared'; ready is slang for cash, so it means obtained cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To encash a cheque is to convert it into money, and ready money is cash in hand.

clue.text: Call to stop unit returning — disgusting!

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: one is a single unit
an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone shouts to halt a returning army unit, appalled.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting the word is an exclamation demanding that something cease because there has been too much of it.

clue.text: Reason for insurance being cancelled initially: too old

indicators.note: the initial letter is cancelled, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: insurance is taken out to provide cover

explanation.surface: An insurer cancels a policy because the customer is too old.
explanation.definitionFit: Over age means beyond the permitted age limit, exceeding the years allowed for something.

clue.text: Change I printed in bold

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A typesetter's note: alter the text I printed into bold type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bold' suggests a typeface, but it means brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and daring, a close synonym for brave or courageous.

clue.text: Fish stew appearing inferior to Brit

indicators.note: in a down clue inferior means lower, so this piece is placed below the next one

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for a British person
to stew is to worry

explanation.surface: Fish stew judged worse than a Brit's cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish stew' looks like a dish, but stew means worry.
explanation.definitionFit: The pomfret is a deep-bodied edible sea fish, both an Atlantic and an Indo-Pacific species.

clue.text: Even if competent, having change of heart over appeal

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, and changing it rearranges those central letters

parts.note: able means competent
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A capable person reconsiders a plea anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters BL swap round; in a down clue the first piece sits over the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Albeit is a conjunction meaning though or although, conceding a point as 'even if' does.

clue.text: What's irregular or oddly regular about one line?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled word goes round the next pieces
arranged oddly means in a strange order, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
standard abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A riddle contrasting the irregular with a regular soldier in the line.
explanation.walkthrough: An irregular is a soldier outside the regular army; the military sense of 'line' and 'regular' adds to the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerrilla fighters are irregulars, members of an unofficial force rather than a national army.

clue.text: Company with help for speaker, often upstanding performer

parts.note: standard abbreviation for company
a microphone helps a speaker be heard

explanation.surface: A firm brings in an amplifier for a respectable entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' sounds like 'honest'; it is a joke on stand-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedian frequently does stand-up, telling jokes on stage while on their feet.

clue.text: Desert ship? Left having arrived earlier

indicators.note: having something earlier means it sits before the next piece in a down entry
earlier says this piece comes first, placed above the other in the down light

parts.note: came means arrived
standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A deserted vessel: it left after arriving earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert ship' looks like abandoning a ship; the question mark flags the nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is called the ship of the desert because it carries loads across sand and sways like a boat.

clue.text: Salutation appropriate for John, Paul, or George, but not Ringo

parts.note: the phrase that would fit as a dedication: to

parts.words: John, Paul, or George, but not Ringo
parts.note: a saint: St John, St Paul and St George exist, but there is no St Ringo

explanation.surface: A tribute fitting three Beatles but not their drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles are a decoy: the names belong to saints, and a dedication reading 'to a St' fits three of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a glass in someone's honour is a salute or tribute, a drinking gesture of greeting.

clue.text: Record hard precious stone cut, in brief

indicators.note: a word that is cut is shortened, so its final letter is lopped off

parts.note: an extended-play record
H for hard, as on pencils
a green gemstone

explanation.surface: A short summary of how a hard gem was cut for a record.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral describes what lasts only a short time, so it is a synonym for fleeting.

clue.text: Recluse found in woman's college in Cambridge

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts

explanation.surface: A shy person discovered in a Cambridge women's college.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge suggests the English university; the college is in the American Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives alone, withdrawn from society, which is what a recluse does.

clue.text: What produces growth in pupil, slow but incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete means missing its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: dilatory means slow, tending to delay

explanation.surface: A teacher's report on a slow learner who is growing anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pupil' suggests a schoolchild; it is the pupil of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilator is a drug or muscle that widens the eye's opening, enlarging the black centre.
